newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean won ends higher on export deals.
newsitem.headline: South Korean won ends higher on export deals.

text.p: The won closed higher versus the dollar on Friday as month-end export negotiations poured in during the afternoon, dealers said.
Shortage of won in the money markets also contributed to the local unit's gain, they said.
The won stood at 819.00 at the closing bell against the opening and intraday low of of 819.70.
"Export deals came in, pushing the dollar to an intraday low of 818.90," said one local dealer.
But the size of month-end export deals were smaller than usual, he said.
Traders said intervention worries continue to buoy the won in a market that is severely short of dollars.
The won is expected to fall on Monday in inactive trading, they said.
"Beginning of the month import deals are likely to boost the dollar," said one trader.
Dealers expect the won to move in a range of 818.50 to 819.80 on Monday with the mid-rate at 819.30/40. Today's mid-rate was pegged at 819.20.
